## 1. Goal

Create the build system and the two shared headers every C file depends on: `core/config.h` (every default and limit) and `core/job.h` (the Job struct, policy enum and error codes). This fixes the names that the rest of the C code and the PRD §5 contract use.

## 2. Background

**From PRD §3 Defaults and limits:**

| Setting | Default | Allowed range | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU capacity | 16 cores | 1 to 1,000,000 | User-editable |
| Memory capacity | 32,768 MB | 1 to 1,000,000,000 | User-editable |
| Priority | — | 0 to 9 | Higher = more important |
| Duration | — | 1 to 1,000,000 ticks | |
| Arrival | — | 0 to 1,000,000,000 ticks | Time stored as 64-bit integers |
| Job id | — | 0 to 2,147,483,647 | Unique within a simulation |
| α (aging rate), stored as `alpha_milli` | 100 (α = 0.1) | 0 to 10,000 (α = 0 to 10) | Integer thousandths of a priority level per tick. 0 turns aging into static priority |
| Reservation threshold T | 50 ticks | 0 to 1,000,000 | 0 reserves immediately |
| Knapsack ε | 0.1 | 0.01 to 1 | Smaller = more accurate, slower |
| Exact solver job limit | 9 | Fixed constant, not configurable | Above this the solver returns `TOO_LARGE` |
| Max jobs, console program | 1,000,000 | | `SimConfig.max_jobs`, set by `cli/main.c` |
| Max jobs, website | 5,000 | | `SimConfig.max_jobs`, set by `wasm/api.c`; keeps the canvas responsive |

**From PRD §3 Build options:**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `make` | Release build of the console program |
| `make debug` | Adds `-g` and turns on invariant checks after every engine step |
| `make sanitize` | Debug build with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer |
| `make test` | Builds and runs all C tests and golden cases |
| `make wasm` | Runs `wasm/build.sh` to produce `web/vendor/aprm.js` |
| `make clean` | Removes build output |

**Emscripten flags (in `wasm/build.sh`).** Modular output with a named factory, single-file output (WebAssembly embedded in the JavaScript), memory growth allowed, and only the step API functions exported. Exact flag spellings are checked against the current Emscripten documentation when the script is written.

**From DECISIONS D13, D27, D51:**

| # | Decision | Reason | Rejected alternatives | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D13 | α is the integer `alpha_milli` (α × 1000, 0–10,000, default 100). Aging key = `1000·b − alpha_milli·r` as int64, overflow-checked. Done before Gate 2 | No floating point in decisions: Clang on Apple Silicon may fuse multiply-add, and rounding could break exact ties, so results would differ across platforms and from hand-worked golden cases | `double alpha` (previous PRD §5); `-ffp-contract=off` alone (still leaves rounding ties) | R1 |
| D27 | `max_jobs` is a field of `SimConfig`: the console program sets 1,000,000, `wasm/api.c` sets 5,000 | The core must know its own limit to return `LIMIT_REACHED` | A compile-time flag per build; an unchecked limit | R1 |
| D51 | The console binary is built to `build/aprm`; `build/` is never committed | One known path for `tools/config.py` and the README | Binary in the repo root | R1 (Step 2 convention) |

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Makefile targets `make`, `make debug`, `make sanitize`, `make test`, `make wasm` (stub until K-13), `make clean`
- Flags `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`; output in `build/`, CLI binary at `build/aprm`
- `core/config.h`: every PRD §3 default and limit as a named constant
- `core/job.h`: `PolicyKind`, `Job`, `SimConfig`, error-code constants from PRD §5
- A tiny assert helper header for C tests and a `make test` loop that runs every `tests/c/test_*.c`

**Out of scope:**

- Any engine logic (K-08, K-09)
- The heap (K-03)
- `wasm/build.sh` (K-13)
- Golden-case runner (K-12)

## 5. Specification

**From PRD §5 Core C functions (types this issue declares):**

```c
typedef enum { POL_FCFS, POL_PRIORITY, POL_SJF, POL_AGING,
               POL_AGING_RESERVE, POL_KNAPSACK } PolicyKind;

typedef struct {
    int64_t cpu_cap, mem_cap;
    PolicyKind policy;
    int64_t alpha_milli;        /* aging rate α × 1000, 0..10000 */
    int64_t reserve_threshold;  /* T, ticks */
    double  knapsack_eps;       /* representation open: DECISIONS O-2 */
    int64_t max_jobs;           /* CLI 1,000,000; website 5,000 */
} SimConfig;

typedef struct {
    int32_t id;
    int64_t arrival, duration, cpu, mem;
    int32_t priority;           /* 0..9 */
} Job;
```

**From PRD §5 Error codes:**

| Code | Name | When | Example message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| -1 | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | Null pointer, bad handle, bad policy | "Unknown policy 9." |
| -2 | `INVALID_FIELD` | A field outside its range (§3); `field` names it | "priority must be 0 to 9." |
| -3 | `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` | Job needs more CPU or memory than the machine has | "Job 4 needs 40960 MB; machine has 32768 MB." |
| -4 | `ARRIVAL_IN_PAST` | Mid-run job with arrival before now | "Arrival 10 is before current time 42." |
| -5 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | Same id added twice | "Job id 3 already exists." |
| -6 | `LIMIT_REACHED` | Too many jobs (§3) | "Website limit is 5000 jobs." |
| -7 | `OUT_OF_MEMORY` | Allocation failed | "Out of memory." |
| -8 | `PARSE_ERROR` | Bad CSV; message gives line and column | "Line 12, column cpu: not a number." |
| -9 | `TOO_LARGE` | Exact solver asked for more than 9 jobs | "Exact solver supports up to 9 jobs." |

Constant names to use in `config.h` (one per PRD §3 row): `APRM_CPU_CAP_DEFAULT 16`, `APRM_CPU_CAP_MIN 1`, `APRM_CPU_CAP_MAX 1000000`, `APRM_MEM_CAP_DEFAULT 32768`, `APRM_MEM_CAP_MIN 1`, `APRM_MEM_CAP_MAX 1000000000`, `APRM_PRIORITY_MIN 0`, `APRM_PRIORITY_MAX 9`, `APRM_DURATION_MIN 1`, `APRM_DURATION_MAX 1000000`, `APRM_ARRIVAL_MIN 0`, `APRM_ARRIVAL_MAX 1000000000`, `APRM_JOB_ID_MAX 2147483647`, `APRM_ALPHA_MILLI_DEFAULT 100`, `APRM_ALPHA_MILLI_MAX 10000`, `APRM_RESERVE_T_DEFAULT 50`, `APRM_RESERVE_T_MAX 1000000`, `APRM_KNAPSACK_EPS_DEFAULT 0.1`, `APRM_KNAPSACK_EPS_MIN 0.01`, `APRM_KNAPSACK_EPS_MAX 1`, `APRM_EXACT_MAX_JOBS 9`, `APRM_MAX_JOBS_CLI 1000000`, `APRM_MAX_JOBS_WEB 5000`.

Error codes in `job.h`: `APRM_OK 0`, `APRM_INVALID_ARGUMENT -1`, `APRM_INVALID_FIELD -2`, `APRM_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED -3`, `APRM_ARRIVAL_IN_PAST -4`, `APRM_DUPLICATE_ID -5`, `APRM_LIMIT_REACHED -6`, `APRM_OUT_OF_MEMORY -7`, `APRM_PARSE_ERROR -8`, `APRM_TOO_LARGE -9`.

Makefile behaviour: `make debug` defines `APRM_DEBUG` (turns on invariant checks after every step, used from K-09); `make sanitize` = debug + `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer`; `make test` builds and runs every `tests/c/test_*.c` and fails on the first failure.

## 6. Step-by-step tasks

1. Write `core/job.h` with the types and error codes above, each with a comment
2. Write `core/config.h` with one constant per PRD §3 row
3. Write `tests/c/test_main.h` (CHECK macro that prints file:line and counts failures)
4. Write the Makefile with the six targets and `build/` output
5. Add `tests/c/test_config.c` and make `make test` run it
6. Run all targets on GCC and Clang

## 9. How to verify

```sh
make clean && make && make debug && make sanitize && make test
CC=clang make clean all test
```
A pass: every command exits 0 with no warnings, and `make test` reports all checks passing.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** one place for every limit and error code, so validation, tests and documentation cannot drift.
**Why integers (`alpha_milli`)?** Scheduling must be identical on every compiler; floating point could differ (DECISIONS D13).
**Examiner question:** "Why `int64_t` for time?" — Arrivals go up to 10⁹ ticks and `start + duration` must never overflow (PRD §3, D28).

## 11. Pitfalls

- Defining constants in two places
- Using `int` for times instead of `int64_t`
- Forgetting `<stdint.h>` in `job.h`
- Putting mutable globals in headers
- A Makefile that only works with GCC flags (test with Clang too)
